title: Perspectives and ethical values
log: 2026-11-12T12:44:18Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: Neither bank point teaches how groups' interests and values shape their perspectives or how geographers weigh values like fairness in a conclusion: the geography card is about justifying a conclusion with evidence, and the English card is about spotting bias in a text.

draft.title: Perspectives and ethical values
card: A perspective is the way a person or group sees an issue. It is shaped by their interests, such as jobs or profit, and by their values, such as caring for nature.
Different groups can look at the same place or plan and reach different views. A farmer, a tourism operator and a local community group may each want something different from the same river.

An ethical value is a belief about what is right or fair, such as fairness to all groups or care for future generations. Geographers can use these values to judge who gains and who loses from a decision.
To justify a conclusion, geographers weigh the perspectives and values involved. They then explain why they favour one outcome, using evidence and naming the values behind their choice.
draft.remember: People see the same issue differently. A sound conclusion weighs those views and the values behind them.

a.q: Why might a fishing business and a conservation group disagree about a new marine park?
opts: They have different interests and values
They are looking at different oceans
One group has no perspective on the issue
Only one group has real evidence available
a.why: A perspective comes from a group's interests and values. The fishing business may care about catch and income, and the conservation group about protecting nature. They can view the same park and still disagree.
a.clue: Think about what each group cares about most.

b.q: A council plans a dam on a river in regional Victoria. Farmers downstream say it would cut their water, while the town upstream wants a secure supply. A geographer recommends sharing the water by need. Which ethical value is the geographer mainly using?
opts: Quickest time to build the dam
b.why: Sharing water by need weighs the claims of both groups, so it is based on fairness. Cost, profit and speed are interests or practical matters, not ethical values about what is right. They do not explain why the water is shared.
b.clue: Which option is a belief about what is right, not a practical matter?

a.best: They have different interests and values
